---
title: "Airhouse"
description: "Oxygen's managed warehouse, where your data lands and is queried from"
---

**Airhouse** is Oxygen's managed warehouse, where your data lands and where
the [semantic model](/guide/build/semantic-model/simple-model) and agents
query it. It speaks the Postgres wire protocol, runs queries on
[DuckDB](https://duckdb.org), and stores tables in open formats with
[DuckLake](https://ducklake.select). It has three parts:

- The **data plane** checks every statement against the caller's credentials,
  role, and limits before DuckDB runs it.
- The **control plane** provisions a database for each workspace and mints
  short-lived credentials on demand.
- **Storage** keeps each database's catalog and Parquet files isolated from
  every other database.

<Frame caption="Airhouse checks every statement before DuckDB runs it, hands out only short-lived credentials, and keeps each database's catalog and files isolated in open formats.">

A highlighted box notes that each database is isolated, with its own catalog, storage prefix, users, and query limits." />

## Why it matters

- **No long-lived keys.** Agents, pipelines, and apps never hold a warehouse
  password. Oxygen mints a credential when one is needed, scoped to the
  caller's role, and it expires on its own.
- **Isolation by default.** Each workspace gets its own database, with its own
  catalog, storage location, users, and query limits.
- **Open formats.** Tables are standard Parquet with a DuckLake catalog, so the
  data stays readable with open tooling and is never locked in.
- **Works with existing tools.** Any Postgres-compatible client or BI tool can
  connect without a new driver.

## Where it fits

[Airway](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airway) pipelines land extracted data
in Airhouse, and [custom apps](/guide/build/sdk/functions) append their own
facts to it. Teams that already run a warehouse can skip Airhouse, since Oxygen
[connects to your own](/guide/build/connect-data) and the semantic model
compiles the same way wherever the data lives.
